advisor.summary: In a 401(k) with employees, the ADP/ACP tests tie the owner's deferrals to what the staff actually defers — low participation sends the owner's contributions back as taxable corrective refunds. A safe harbor design buys out the tests: commit to a 3% nonelective contribution for all eligibles or a matching formula costing up to 4% of participating pay under §401(k)(12) (QACA auto-enrollment variants under §401(k)(13)), and the owner defers the full $24,500 for 2026 plus catch-up regardless of staff behavior. The nonelective route also supplies most of the cross-testing gateway, which makes it the default foundation for every owner-max stacked design. This is an enabling strategy — the deduction it unlocks is modeled under the deferral and profit-sharing records, not here.
mechanics: The ADP and ACP tests of §§401(k)(3), 401(m) cap HCE deferral rates at a spread over the NHCE average — with minimal staff participation, an owner targeting a full deferral fails badly and receives corrective refunds as taxable income.

The §401(k)(12) buy-out options: a 3% nonelective contribution to every eligible employee regardless of participation, or the basic match — 100% of the first 3% deferred plus 50% of the next 2%, a maximum cost of 4% of pay and only for those who defer; §401(k)(13) QACA variants trade automatic enrollment for a slightly cheaper formula and two-year vesting.
Safe harbor dollars are immediately 100% vested (QACA's two-year cliff excepted) — they leave with departing employees, with no forfeiture recapture.

The 3% nonelective typically supplies most of the 5% cross-testing gateway, so it is the default chassis when a new comparability or cash balance layer is planned; the match design does not count toward the gateway.

Timing under SECURE Act §103: match designs need provisions and the participant notice in place before the plan year, but a 3% nonelective can be adopted retroactively until 30 days before plan year-end — or through the close of the following year at 4% — so a failed ADP year can literally be repaired after the fact.

authority.note: The ADP and ACP nondiscrimination tests the safe harbor design buys out.
The traditional safe harbor formulas: 3% nonelective or the basic match, both immediately vested.
The QACA automatic-enrollment safe harbor with a reduced match formula and two-year vesting.
Removed the notice requirement for nonelective safe harbors and created the retroactive adoption windows — 3% until 30 days before year-end, 4% through the following year.
The 2026 deferral limit ($24,500) and catch-up amounts the design unlocks for the owner.

requirements: At least one non-owner employee in the plan — owner-only plans have no ADP test, so safe harbor adds nothing there.
A budget commitment of 3% of all eligible compensation (nonelective) or up to 4% of participating payroll (match) for every year the design runs.
A plan amendment, plus the annual participant notice before the plan year for match designs.
Payroll integration that computes and deposits the safe harbor amounts correctly.
risks: The recurring compliance failure is timing and notice: a match design with a late or missing participant notice loses safe harbor status for the year, resurrecting the very tests the client paid to escape.
Mid-year suspension of safe harbor contributions is available only in narrow circumstances and re-triggers full-year ADP testing — treat the funding as an annual commitment.

Choosing the match to save money can foreclose the stack: the match does not satisfy the cross-testing gateway, and owners who later want profit-sharing or cash balance layers usually wish they had bought the 3% nonelective — design for the end state.
Immediate vesting means safe harbor dollars walk out the door with short-tenure employees.
stateNotes: Employer safe harbor contributions are ordinary deductible compensation costs in every state that conforms to federal taxable income or federal AGI — the standard case; verify only in non-conformity outliers.
PTET interaction: the contribution reduces pass-through income before any PTET election is computed, so it belongs in the PTET estimate like any other deductible cost.
Missouri conforms through RSMo §143.121; for Missouri SALT Parity Act electors (RSMo §143.436), the safe harbor cost lowers the PTET base dollar for dollar.
reviewChecklist: Last ADP/ACP test results pulled and the owner's current refund exposure quantified before recommending.
Formula chosen against the end-state design — nonelective if any profit-sharing or cash balance stacking is plausible — not just current-year cost.
Amendment executed and, for match designs, the participant notice calendared and delivered before the plan year.
SECURE Act §103 retroactive adoption windows checked when the year is already underway.
Owner deferral election raised to the maximum once testing relief is in place.

client.teaser: Stop the IRS test that keeps sending your 401(k) money back.
client.headline: Unlock your full 401(k) — no matter what your employees save
plainEnglish: Here is a rule many owners learn the hard way. In a company 401(k), the IRS ties what YOU can save to what your employees choose to save. If your team saves little, your own money gets sent back to you — and taxed.

The fix is a safe harbor design. Your business commits to a modest, set contribution for employees — about 3 to 4 percent of pay. In exchange, the IRS turns the test off. You can save the full legal limit every year, no matter what anyone else does.
The employee money is not wasted. It is a real benefit your team can see, it is fully deductible, and it often doubles as the base for larger owner-focused designs we may add later.
client.analogy: It is like paying a flat toll for the express lane all year. A small known cost — and you never sit in traffic you cannot control.
benefits: Save your full 401(k) limit every year, with no test to fail
A small, known cost instead of surprise refunds at tax time
A visible benefit that helps you hire and keep good people
Sets the base for the bigger owner-focused plan designs
steps: WE pull your plan's test results and show what the cap costs you now.
WE pick the right version — flat contribution or match — for where your plan is headed.
WE update the plan documents and handle the employee notice.
YOU raise your own savings to the full limit from then on.
clientCommitments: Fund the employee contribution every year the design is in place
Get payroll data to the plan team on time
Flag big staffing changes so we can re-check the design

annualMaintenance: Annual participant notice (match designs) and funding verification
Year-end check that safe harbor deposits reconcile with payroll
Design review when staffing or stacking plans change
deliverables: Plan amendment adopting the safe harbor provisions
Cost comparison memo: nonelective versus match against the end-state design
Participant notice template and compliance calendar
